<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard AUR package build process for `opencomposite-git`, a reimplementation of OpenVR that translates calls to OpenXR. The source arrays correctly reference the project's own upstream GitLab repository and several well-known, legitimate upstream dependencies (OpenXR-SDK, glm, libunwind) via HTTPS from GitHub. All checksums are set to "SKIP", which is expected and acceptable for VCS-based packages in AUR, especially when tracking mutable branches like `openxr`. This does not indicate malice, only that the sources are not pinned to a specific commit in the PKGBUILD — a common practice for -git packages.

The `prepare()` function configures Git submodules to use local directories for dependencies, which were cloned as part of the `source` array. This is a normal technique to avoid redundant network requests and ensure submodule resolution during build. The use of `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update` is safe here because the submodule URLs are explicitly set to local paths, preventing arbitrary remote code execution. The build uses standard CMake invocations, and the `package()` function installs only built binaries and a configuration file into the package directory, with no unexpected file operations or system modifications.

No obfuscated code, network exfiltration, or dangerous commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, or base64-encoded payloads) are present. All operations align with standard AUR packaging practices for a C++ project with submodules. The package does not install systemd services, modify system configuration, or access sensitive user data. While the use of mutable branches reduces reproducibility, it does not constitute a security threat on its own.
</details>
